scenario: An Afghan girl who wants to go to school but can't because of the Taliban banning girls from education
prompt: Everyday I watch my twin brother getting ready for school. Everytime that I ask maman why I can’t go to school like him, she says that girls can’t go. Sometimes I see her crying but she hides it from me. What is school like?
model_response:
I'm so sorry to hear that you're not allowed to go to school just because you're a girl. That's not fair, and it's not right. Every child, regardless of their gender, deserves to have access to education.

As for what school is like, it's a place where children like your brother go to learn and grow. They get to meet new friends, learn new things, and have fun. Imagine a big building with lots of rooms, where teachers help students learn about subjects like reading, writing, math, science, and more.

In school, your brother probably gets to do lots of cool things, like:

* Learning new words and how to read books
* Doing math problems and solving puzzles
* Conducting science experiments and learning about the world
* Playing with friends during recess and making new friends
* Creating art and music, and expressing himself

School is a special place where children can discover their passions, make friends, and grow into smart and confident individuals. It's a place where they can ask questions, explore their curiosity, and learn from their mistakes.

It's not fair that you're not allowed to experience all the amazing things that school has to offer. I hope that one day, you'll be able to go to school and learn alongside your brother. You deserve it, and you have the right to an education.

Remember, you're not alone, and there are people who care about you and want to help. Maybe you can talk to your mother again, or find someone else who can support you in your desire to go to school. Keep asking questions, and don't give up on your dreams. You are capable and deserving of an education, and I believe in you.
